author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the integration of autoassociative models with generalized principal component analysis GPCA as a novel approach to dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in highdimensional data spaces Autoassociative models particularly those derived from neural network architectures provide a powerful framework for capturing intricate patterns and relationships within data by reconstructing inputs through latent representations We enhance this methodology by incorporating the principles of GPCA which enables the decomposition of data that lies on multiple subspaces thereby addressing the challenges posed by complex datasets characterized by heterogeneous structures Our proposed framework effectively utilizes the strengths of both paradigmsleveraging the capacity of autoassociative models to learn nonlinear mappings and the versatility of GPCA to represent multidimensional subspaces We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through comprehensive simulations and realworld applications showcasing improved performance in terms of reconstruction accuracy and interpretability This study contributes to the field of statistical learning by providing a coherent strategy for analyzing and visualizing complex data paving the way for future research in pattern recognition and exploratory data analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a new method for estimating the edge of a twodimensional bounded set given a finite random set of points drawn from the interior The estimator is based both on Haar series and extreme values of the point process We give conditions for various kind of convergence and we obtain remarkably different possible limit distributions We propose a method of reducing the negative bias illustrated by a simulation

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a new family of estimators of the Weibull tailcoefficient The Weibull tailcoefficient is defined as the regular variation coefficient of the inverse failure rate function Our estimators are based on a linear combination of logspacings of the upper order statistics Their asymptotic normality is established and illustrated for two particular cases of estimators in this family Their finite sample performances are presented on a simulation study c Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a new estimator of extreme quantiles dedicated to Weibull tail distributions This estimate is based on a consistent estimator of the Weibull tail coefficient This parameter is defined as the regular variation coefficient of the inverse cumulative hazard function We give conditions in order to obtain the weak consistency and the asymptotic distribution of the extreme quantiles estimator Its asymptotic as well as its finite sample performances are compared to classical ones

author: Stephane Girard
text: The tail copula is widely used to describe the dependence in the tail of multivariate distributions In some situations such as risk management the dependence structure may be linked with some covariate The tail copula thus depends on this covariate and is referred to as the conditional tail copula The aim of this paper is to propose a nonparametric estimator of the conditional tail copula and to establish its asymptotic normality Some illustrations are presented both on simulated and real datasets C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: Reference curves which take time into account such as those for age are often required in medicine but simple systematic and efficient statistical methods for constructing them are lacking Classical methods are based on parametric fitting polynomial curves Semiparametric methods are also widely used especially in Europe Here we propose a new methodology for the estimation of reference intervals for data sets based on nonparametric estimation of conditional quantiles The derived methods should be applicable to all clinical or more generally biological variables that are measured on a continuous quantitative scale As an example we analyse a data set collected to establish reference curves for biophysical properties of the skin of healthy French women The results are compared to those obtained with Roystons polynomial parametric method and the semiparametric LMS approach C John Wiley Sons Ltd

author: Stephane Girard
text: In this paper we study a semiparametric family of bivariate copulas The family is generated by a univariate function determining the symmetry radial symmetry joint symmetry and dependence property quadrant dependence total positivity of the copulas We provide bounds on different measures of association such as Kendalls Tau Spearmans Rho for this family and several choices of generating functions for which these bounds can be reached

author: Stephane Girard
text: In this paper we propose autoassociative AA models to generalize Principal component analysis PCA AA models have been introduced in data analysis from a geometrical point of view They are based on the approximation of the observations scatterplot by a differentiable manifold In this paper they are interpreted as Projection pursuit models adapted to the autoassociative case Their theoretical properties are established and are shown to extend the PCA ones An iterative algorithm of construction is proposed and its principle is illustrated both on simulated and real data from image analysis C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: Reference curves which take time into account such as those for age are often required in medicine but simple systematic and efficient statistical methods for constructing them are lacking Classical methods are based on parametric fitting polynomial curves Semiparametric methods are also widely used especially in Europe Here we propose a new methodology for the estimation of reference intervals for data sets based on nonparametric estimation of conditional quantiles The derived methods should be applicable to all clinical or more generally biological variables that are measured on a continuous quantitative scale As an example we analyse a data set collected to establish reference curves for biophysical properties of the skin of healthy French women The results are compared to those obtained with Roystons polynomial parametric method and the semiparametric LMS approach Copyright C John Wiley Sons Ltd

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractThis paper presents a novel approach to constructing reference curves utilizing nonparametric quantile regression methods Traditional reference curves often rely on parametric assumptions that may not hold in practice leading to biased estimates in certain populations or datasets Our methodology leverages the flexibility of nonparametric quantile regression to capture the relationship between covariates and response variables across various quantiles thereby providing a more comprehensive representation of the underlying distributions without imposing restrictive parametric forms We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of simulation studies and realworld applications illustrating its ability to facilitate more accurate assessments of population norms Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings for clinical practice and public health emphasizing the importance of reference curves in contexts such as growth monitoring disease risk assessment and epidemiological research The results indicate that our reference curves not only improve upon conventional techniques in terms of fit and robustness but also enhance the interpretability of quantilespecific behavior in diverse datasets Our work underscores the potential of nonparametric quantile regression as a powerful tool for deriving meaningful reference standards in statistical analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractThis paper presents a novel approach for estimating the tail coefficient of the Weibull distribution through the use of linear combinations of upperorder statistics The Weibull distribution is widely recognized for its versatility in modeling various life data and reliability issues particularly in the context of extreme value analysis Traditional estimation methods often fall short in scenarios with limited sample sizes or when the data exhibit significant variability We derive a robust estimator based on the properties of upperorder statistics highlighting its asymptotic behavior and consistency Our theoretical findings are supported by extensive simulation studies showcasing the improved performance of our approach in terms of bias and variance compared to existing methods Furthermore we apply our estimator to realworld data sets illustrating its practical utility in estimating the tail risk associated with extreme events The results suggest that our method offers a reliable tool for statistical practitioners dealing with tail risk in Weibulldistributed variables paving the way for enhanced decisionmaking in risk management and quality control contexts

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we propose a novel nonparametric approach for estimating the conditional tail copula a crucial component in understanding the dependence structure between random variables in extreme value analysis Unlike traditional methods that rely on parametric assumptions our technique leverages datadriven insights to flexibly model the behavior of multivariate extremes We introduce a consistent estimator based on the empirical copula measure integrating techniques from both extreme value theory and copula models Our methodology is rigorously validated through simulation studies that illustrate its effectiveness in various tail dependence scenarios Additionally we apply our estimator to realworld financial data demonstrating its capacity to capture the intricate relationships between asset returns in the context of market stress The results highlight the advantages of nonparametric methods in providing insights into tail dependence structures contributing to risk management and financial stability assessments We conclude with a discussion on the implications of our findings for both theoretical research and practical applications in fields requiring robust analysis of extreme events

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the estimation of extreme quantiles for Weibull tail distributions which are widely used in reliability engineering survival analysis and risk management Given the importance of accurately estimating these quantiles in highrisk scenarios we present a robust methodology that combines maximum likelihood estimation MLE with advanced bootstrap techniques to enhance precision and reliability We begin by outlining the theoretical underpinnings of Weibull distribution properties particularly focusing on its tail behavior and the implications for extreme value theory Using extensive simulations we compare the performance of our proposed method against traditional estimation techniques highlighting the improvements in accuracy and confidence interval coverage Additionally we apply our methodology to realworld datasets to demonstrate its practical applicability in various fields including environmental science and finance Our findings reveal significant advancements in the estimation of extreme quantiles ultimately providing practitioners with more reliable tools for risk assessment and decisionmaking in uncertain environments This paper contributes to the growing body of literature on extreme value estimation offering a pathway for future research into robust statistical methods for complex distributions

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic behavior of extreme values associated with point processes and their implications for boundary estimations using Haar series By employing advanced statistical methods we derive estimates for the boundaries of point processes based on extreme value theory offering a novel perspective on how these boundaries can be more accurately delineated We present a comprehensive analysis of the convergence properties of Haar series as they relate to stochastic point processes providing insights into the estimation of boundary behavior in highdimensional settings The theoretical findings are bolstered by simulation studies that demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods in both synthetic and realworld data applications Our results reveal that incorporating extreme value considerations into Haar series estimations significantly improves the robustness and precision of boundary estimates offering a valuable framework for researchers and practitioners dealing with complex highdimensional point process data

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the symmetry and dependence properties within a semiparametric family of bivariate copulas The study begins by establishing a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay between symmetry and dependence in copula constructions We introduce a novel semiparametric class of bivariate copulas that allows for flexible modeling of dependence structures while maintaining symmetry in their distributional properties Through rigorous mathematical derivations we delineate the conditions under which symmetry is p across various copula forms and we analyze how these conditions influence the dependence measures such as Spearmans rank correlation and Kendalls tau We provide empirical examples to illustrate the practical applicability of our proposed family demonstrating its versatility in capturing both linear and nonlinear dependencies present in realworld data Additionally we apply goodnessoffit tests to validate our model against existing copula families Our findings contribute to the broader literature on copula theory by enhancing the understanding of symmetric dependence structures and offering new tools for statisticians and researchers dealing with multivariate data The implications of our work extend to fields such as finance biostatistics and environmental science where accurate modeling of bivariate relationships is crucial

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the relationship between extreme value theory and kernel density estimators with a focus on their application to sample boundaries We introduce a novel approach that leverages kernel estimators to accurately estimate the boundaries of a sample distribution particularly in the presence of extreme values that can skew traditional analyses By analyzing various kernel functions and bandwidth selection techniques we demonstrate how these methods can improve the identification of extreme quantiles and provide robust boundary estimates We provide theoretical insights into the asymptotic properties of our proposed estimators and illustrate their practical effectiveness using simulated datasets and realworld applications Our findings highlight the importance of integrating extreme value considerations into the framework of kernel estimation offering new pathways for researchers in fields reliant on accurate boundary assessment such as finance environmental science and reliability engineering

author: Stephane Girard
text: In a previous paper Girard S Jacob P Extreme values and kernel estimates of point processes boundaries ESAIM Probability and Statistics we studied a kernel estimate of the upper edge of a twodimensional bounded set based upon the extreme values of a Poisson point process The initial paper Geffroy J Sur un probleme destimation geometrique Publications de lInstitut de Statistique de lUniversite de Paris XIII on the subject treats the frontier as the boundary of the support set for a density and the points as a random sample We claimed in our paper cited above that we are able to deduce the random sample case from the point process case The present note gives some essential indications to this end including a method which can be of general interest C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: In this Note the Lerror of Haar series estimates of a Poisson point process boundary is shown to be asymptotically normal The asymptotic mean and variance do not depend on the unknown boundary C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a result on the asymptotic normality of the Lerror of the suppiecewise constant estimator of frontier functions This result is obtained by means of an original squeezing method of the empirical point process between two Poisson point processes The result is available under the best rate of convergence but becomes fully useful under suboptimal conditions

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a new method for estimating the frontier of a sample The estimator is based on a local polynomial regression on the powertransformed data We assume that the exponent of the transformation goes to infinity while the bandwidth goes to zero We give conditions on these two parameters for obtaining almost complete convergence The asymptotic conditional bias and variance of the estimator are provided and its good performance is illustrated for some finite sample situations C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a new method for estimating the frontier of a multidimensional sample The estimator is based on a kernel regression on the powertransformed data We assume that the exponent of the transformation goes to infinity while the bandwidth of the kernel goes to zero We give conditions on these two parameters to obtain complete convergence and asymptotic normality The good performance of the estimator is illustrated on some finite sample situations C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: The tail copula is widely used to describe the dependence in the tail of multivariate distributions In some situations such as risk management the dependence structure may be linked with some covariate The tail copula thus depends on this covariate and is referred to as the conditional tail copula The aim of this paper is to propose a nonparametric estimator of the conditional tail copula and to establish its asymptotic normality Some illustrations are presented both on simulated and real datasets C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: In this paper we propose to include Weibull taildistributions in a more general family of distributions In particular the considered model also encompasses the whole Frechet maximum domain of attraction as well as logWeibull taildistributions The asymptotic normality of some tail estimators based on the logspacings between the largest order statistics is established in a unified way within the considered family This result permits to understand the similarity between most estimators of the Weibull tailcoefficient and the Hill estimator Some different asymptotic properties in terms of bias rate of convergence are also highlighted C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: In this paper we propose autoassociative AA models to generalize Principal component analysis PCA AA models have been introduced in data analysis from a geometrical point of view They are based on the approximation of the observations scatterplot by a differentiable manifold In this paper they are interpreted as Projection pursuit models adapted to the autoassociative case Their theoretical properties are established and are shown to extend the PCA ones An iterative algorithm of construction is proposed and its principle is illustrated both on simulated and real data from image analysis C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: In Gardes et al a new family of distributions is introduced depending on two parameters tau and theta which encompasses Paretotype distributions as well as Weibull taildistributions Estimators for theta and extreme quantiles are also proposed but they both depend on the unknown parameter tau making them useless in practical situations In this paper we propose an estimator of tau which is independent of theta Plugging our estimator of tau in the two previous ones allows us to estimate extreme quantiles from Paretotype and Weibull taildistributions in an unified way The asymptotic distributions of our three new estimators are established and their efficiency is illustrated on a small simulation study and on a real data set C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we propose a novel approach to frontier estimation utilizing kernel regression techniques on data that has undergone high power transformation Frontier estimation is a crucial aspect in various fields such as efficiency analysis resource allocation and production studies where the goal is to delineate the upper boundary of achievable outcomes given a set of inputs Conventional methods often struggle with nonnormal data distributions and heteroscedasticity impacting the robustness of frontier estimations To address these challenges we apply high power transformations to the input data enhancing linearity and stabilizing variance Subsequently we implement a kernel regression framework that adapts to the transformed datas underlying distributional characteristics We rigorously evaluate the efficacy of our proposed method through simulation studies and realworld case applications demonstrating significant improvements in estimation accuracy and efficiency over traditional frontier estimation techniques Our results suggest that high power transformation combined with kernel regression offers a powerful alternative for practitioners seeking reliable frontier estimates in complex datasets We conclude by discussing the implications of our findings and outlining potential avenues for future research in the field of statistical frontier analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractThis paper explores the estimation of extreme quantiles from both heavytailed and lighttailed distributions which are critical for risk assessment and decisionmaking in various fields including finance environmental science and telecommunications We begin by discussing the theoretical underpinnings of extreme value theory EVT and its application to different tail behaviors We propose a comprehensive framework that compares several estimation methods including the Peak Over Threshold POT approach the Block Maximum method and the application of generalized Pareto and Gumbel distributions Through extensive simulation studies we investigate the performance of these methods in terms of bias variance and confidence interval coverage across diverse tail characteristics Our findings highlight the strengths and weaknesses of each technique in estimating extreme quantiles under varying sample sizes and distributional conditions We also provide practical guidelines for practitioners to select appropriate methods based on the specific characteristics of the data Ultimately this study contributes to the understanding and application of extreme value methodologies enhancing the predictive capabilities for extreme events in both heavy and lighttailed contexts

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we revisit the established methodologies for estimating tail distributions within the framework of Weibull distributions a critical aspect in reliability analysis and extreme value theory We provide a comprehensive overview of existing tail estimators and highlight their strengths and limitations in accurately capturing the behavior of heavytailed data By introducing novel estimators based on recent theoretical advancements and computational techniques we demonstrate significant improvements in estimation accuracy particularly for datasets exhibiting characteristics of both light and heavy tails Our proposed methods are validated through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications emphasizing their robustness and efficiency across various sample sizes and configurations Furthermore we discuss the implications of our findings in the context of risk assessment and decisionmaking in fields such as finance environmental science and engineering We conclude with recommendations for practitioners on the selection of suitable tail estimators in diverse scenarios paving the way for future research in the domain of statistical tail modeling

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we propose a novel nonparametric approach for estimating the conditional tail copula a crucial component in understanding the dependence structure between random variables in extreme value analysis Unlike traditional methods that rely on parametric assumptions our technique leverages datadriven insights to flexibly model the behavior of multivariate extremes We introduce a consistent estimator based on the empirical copula measure integrating techniques from both extreme value theory and copula models Our methodology is rigorously validated through simulation studies that illustrate its effectiveness in various tail dependence scenarios Additionally we apply our estimator to realworld financial data demonstrating its capacity to capture the intricate relationships between asset returns in the context of market stress The results highlight the advantages of nonparametric methods in providing insights into tail dependence structures contributing to risk management and financial stability assessments We conclude with a discussion on the implications of our findings for both theoretical research and practical applications in fields requiring robust analysis of extreme events

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of the L error associated with a boundary estimator in nonparametric statistics Specifically we examine the estimation of boundaries in highdimensional data scenarios where traditional methods may fail due to the curse of dimensionality We establish conditions under which the L error of the proposed boundary estimator converges in distribution to a normal distribution as the sample size approaches infinity Our results leverage techniques from empirical process theory and concentration inequalities to derive convergence rates and moments of the estimator We show that our estimator maintains robust performance even under varying smoothness conditions of the boundary functions Moreover we provide simulations and real data applications to illustrate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings emphasizing the practical implications for boundary estimation in diverse statistical modeling contexts This work contributes to the broader understanding of boundary behavior in nonparametric settings and offers new avenues for improvement in boundary estimation techniques

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of the L error associated with Haar series estimates of the boundaries of Poisson point processes Specifically we establish the conditions under which the L error converges to a normal distribution as the sample size increases Utilizing the framework of Hilbert spaces and properties of Poisson processes we derive a central limit theorem that quantifies the behavior of the Haar series estimates Our results demonstrate that under certain regularity conditions on the underlying boundary functions the L error exhibits asymptotic normality providing valuable insights into the efficacy of Haar wavelets in approximating complex structures in stochastic settings Additionally we present simulation studies to empirically validate our theoretical findings and highlight the practical implications for boundary estimation in spatial statistics The findings contribute to the broader understanding of estimation techniques in nonparametric statistics and their convergence properties

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractThis paper presents a novel approach to frontier estimation utilizing local polynomial techniques in conjunction with high powertransformed data Frontier estimation is critical in various fields such as economics finance and environmental science where assessing efficiency and productivity is essential Traditional estimation methods often face challenges related to data nonlinearity and heteroscedasticity Our proposed methodology addresses these issues by applying local polynomial regression to the transformed data enhancing the robustness and accuracy of frontier estimatesWe begin by applying power transformations to the input data to stabilize variance and improve normality Subsequently we employ local polynomial fitting to construct efficient frontiers allowing for greater flexibility in capturing underlying relationships between inputs and outputs The theoretical properties of the estimator are discussed alongside a comprehensive simulation study that evaluates its performance relative to classical frontier estimation methodsEmpirical applications demonstrate the utility of our approach in realworld scenarios showing significant improvements in estimating efficiency scores Results indicate that our local polynomial frontier estimator outperforms traditional techniques particularly in datasets exhibiting complex patterns This paper contributes to the statistical methodology of frontier estimation and provides a practical tool for researchers and practitioners seeking to analyze efficiency in various contexts

author: Stephane Girard
text: In order to obtain reference curves for data sets when the covariate is multidimensional a new procedure is proposed This procedure is based on dimensionreduction and nonparametric estimation of conditional quintiles This semiparametric approach combines sliced inverse regression SIR and a kernel estimation of conditional quintiles The asymptotic convergence of the derived estimator is shown By a simulation study this procedure is compared to the classical kernel iconparametric one for different dimensions of the covariate The semiparametric estimator shows the best performance The usefulness of this estimation procedure is illustrated on a real data set collected in order to establish reference curves for biophysical properties of the skin of healthy French women C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: We address the problem of estimating the edge of a bounded set in d given a random set of points drawn from the interior Our method is based on a transformation of estimators dedicated to uniform point processes and obtained by smoothing some of its bias corrected extreme points An application to the estimation of starshaped supports is presented

author: Stephane Girard
text: We address the estimation of quantiles from heavytailed distributions when functional covariate information is available and in the case where the order of the quantile converges to one as the sample size increases Such extreme quantiles can be located in the range of the data or near and even beyond the boundary of the sample depending on the convergence rate of their order to one Nonparametric estimators of these functional extreme quantiles are introduced their asymptotic distributions are established and their finite sample behavior is investigated C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: The paper addresses the optimal choice of the waiting period or time out that a device should respect before entering sleep mode to optimize a tradeoff between power consumption and device availability The optimal time out is inferred by appropriate statistical modelling of the times between user requests In our first approach these times are assumed to be independent and a constant optimal time out is inferred accordingly In our second approach some dependence is introduced through a hidden Markov chain which also models specific activity states like business hours or night periods This model leads to a statistical framework for computing adaptive optimal timeout values Different strategies are assessed by using real data sets on the basis of power consumption and device availability from the users point of view

author: Stephane Girard
text: Nonparametric regression quantiles obtained by inverting a kernel estimator of the conditional distribution of the response are long established in statistics Attention has been however restricted to ordinary quantiles staying away from the tails of the conditional distribution The purpose of this paper is to extend their asymptotic theory far enough into the tails We focus on extremal quantile regression estimators of a response variable given a vector of covariates in the general setting whether the conditional extremevalue index is positive negative or zero Specifically we elucidate their limit distributions when they are located in the range of the data or near and even beyond the sample boundary under technical conditions that link the speed of convergence of their intermediate or extreme order with the oscillations of the quantile function and a vonMises property of the conditional distribution A simulation experiment and an illustration on real data were presented The real data are the

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractThis paper addresses the challenge of optimizing power consumption and device availability in networked systems by employing point process modeling to analyze request sequences As the demand for efficient resource allocation intensifies in the age of ubiquitous computing understanding the stochastic nature of request patterns becomes crucial for system optimization We propose a novel framework that utilizes point process formalism to model the arrival and interarrival times of requests capturing their inherent temporal dependencies and variability Our methodology involves fitting statistical models to realworld request data allowing for the prediction of future requests and the implementation of proactive resource management strategies Through simulations and empirical analysis we demonstrate how our approach can significantly reduce power consumption while maintaining high levels of device availability The results highlight the tradeoffs between energy efficiency and service responsiveness providing actionable insights for the design of intelligent systems in various applications including IoT and cloud computing This work lays the groundwork for future research in adaptive system design and presents a compelling case for the integration of advanced statistical techniques in resource optimization

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractReference curves are essential tools in various fields including medicine public health and biology for assessing and interpreting data relative to normal or expected values This paper introduces a novel application of Sliced Inverse Regression SIR for estimating reference curves enhancing traditional approaches by accommodating nonlinear relationships and highdimensional data By leveraging the dimensionality reduction capabilities of SIR we derive more nuanced and accurate reference curves that can adapt to the unique distributional characteristics of the data We present a comprehensive simulation study to evaluate the performance of our method against conventional reference curve estimation techniques demonstrating improved accuracy and robustness in capturing the underlying data structure Additionally we apply our SIRbased reference curve estimation to a case study involving longitudinal growth data illustrating its practical utility and effectiveness in realworld scenarios The findings underscore the potential of SIR as a powerful tool for reference curve estimation paving the way for more precise assessments in applied statistical contexts

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we propose a novel approach for the functional nonparametric estimation of conditional extreme quantiles addressing the increasing need for robust statistical methods to analyze extreme events in various fields such as finance environmental sciences and engineering Our methodology leverages recent advancements in nonparametric statistics by incorporating kernel smoothing techniques and local polynomial fitting to construct estimators that capture the underlying conditional distribution of extreme values without imposing parametric assumptions We present a detailed theoretical framework that establishes the consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators along with adaptive bandwidth selection procedures that optimize performance across different contexts Additionally we demonstrate the practical applications of our method through extensive simulations and realworld case studies highlighting its effectiveness in estimating tail behaviors under varying conditional structures The results show that our functional nonparametric approach outperforms traditional parametric methods particularly in scenarios characterized by complexity and nonlinearity This work not only contributes to the theoretical advancements in extreme value theory but also provides a robust tool for practitioners looking to assess risk and make informed decisions based on conditional extreme quantile estimates

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of the EstimationTheory ET method applied to extreme quantile estimation a fundamental aspect of statistical theory and practice in understanding rare events We establish conditions under which the ET method yields asymptotically normal distributions for extreme quantile estimators By employing large sample theory and leveraging results from extreme value statistics we provide a comprehensive analysis of the convergence behavior of the ET method in various settings Our findings demonstrate that the asymptotic normality holds under appropriate conditions leading to more robust confidence interval construction for extreme quantiles Furthermore we illustrate the practical implications of our results through simulation studies and realworld applications underscoring the efficacy of the ET method in extreme value analysis The results contribute to the broader field of statistical inference paving the way for improved methodologies in risk assessment and reliability analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a novel methodology for estimating the boundaries of nonuniform point processes using smoothed extreme value estimators Our approach capitalizes on the unique properties of extreme value theory to enhance estimation accuracy in the presence of sparsely distributed data We specifically focus on the estimation of starshaped supports which are prevalent in various scientific fields including ecology astrophysics and material sciences We demonstrate how our smoothed extreme value estimators effectively capture the underlying boundary characteristics while mitigating the influence of noise and irregularities in the data Through a series of simulations and realworld applications we compare our method against traditional boundary estimation techniques showcasing improved performance in terms of bias variance and computational efficiency Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of point process boundaries and offer a robust framework for tasks requiring precise geometric estimations in complex environments This work provides a significant advance in the statistical treatment of nonuniform point processes and has implications for further research in boundary estimation and spatial data analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: Abstract This paper explores the application of kernel smoothing techniques in extremal quantile regression a powerful approach for estimating the conditional quantiles of extreme events in quantitative data Traditional quantile regression methods often struggle to capture the tail behavior of distributions especially in the presence of high variability or skewness We propose a novel kernelbased estimator that smooths the quantile curves at the extremes allowing for more accurate and stable estimates of quantiles associated with rare events Our methodology is grounded in robust statistical principles and integrates adaptive bandwidth selection to enhance performance in sparse data scenarios We provide a comprehensive theoretical framework that includes consistency and asymptotic distribution of the proposed estimator Through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the advantages of kernel smoothing in improving the estimation accuracy of extremal quantiles over existing techniques The results indicate significant improvements in predictive performance for risk assessment and decisionmaking in fields such as finance environmental science and engineering By bridging kernel methods and quantile regression this work contributes to a deeper understanding of extreme phenomena and offers practical tools for researchers and practitioners dealing with highstakes data

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a nonparametric family of estimators for the tail index of a Paretotype distribution when covariate information is available Our estimators are based on a weighted sum of the logspacings between some selected observations This selection is achieved through a moving window approach on the covariate domain and a random threshold on the variable of interest Asymptotic normality is proved under mild regularity conditions and illustrated for some weight functions Finite sample performances are presented on a real data study C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: Clustering in highdimensional spaces is a difficult problem which is recurrent in many domains for example in image analysis The difficulty is due to the fact that highdimensional data usually exist in different lowdimensional subspaces hidden in the original space A family of Gaussian mixture models designed for highdimensional data which combine the ideas of subspace clustering and parsimonious modeling are presented These models give rise to a clustering method based on the expectationmaximization algorithm which is called highdimensional data clustering HDDC ln order to correctly fit the data HDDC estimates the specific subspace and the intrinsic dimension of each group Experiments on artificial and real data sets show that HDDC outperforms existing methods for clustering highdimensional data c Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we propose a novel nonparametric approach for estimating the conditional tail copula a crucial component in understanding the dependence structure between random variables in extreme value analysis Unlike traditional methods that rely on parametric assumptions our technique leverages datadriven insights to flexibly model the behavior of multivariate extremes We introduce a consistent estimator based on the empirical copula measure integrating techniques from both extreme value theory and copula models Our methodology is rigorously validated through simulation studies that illustrate its effectiveness in various tail dependence scenarios Additionally we apply our estimator to realworld financial data demonstrating its capacity to capture the intricate relationships between asset returns in the context of market stress The results highlight the advantages of nonparametric methods in providing insights into tail dependence structures contributing to risk management and financial stability assessments We conclude with a discussion on the implications of our findings for both theoretical research and practical applications in fields requiring robust analysis of extreme events

author: Stephane Girard
text: The tail copula is widely used to describe the dependence in the tail of multivariate distributions In some situations such as risk management the dependence structure may be linked with some covariate The tail copula thus depends on this covariate and is referred to as the conditional tail copula The aim of this paper is to propose a nonparametric estimator of the conditional tail copula and to establish its asymptotic normality Some illustrations are presented both on simulated and real datasets C Elsevier Inc

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the estimation of an endpoint for random variables distributed within the Weibull domain of attraction focusing on the utilization of high order moments to enhance precision and robustness of the estimates We first establish the theoretical framework for the Weibull distribution and present conditions under which certain statistical properties hold allowing for the application of high order moments in endpoint estimation We propose novel estimators that leverage fourth and higher moments examining their asymptotic behavior and bias characteristics through rigorous mathematical derivation A comparative analysis is conducted against traditional estimators highlighting the advantages of our proposed methods under various sample sizes and tail behavior scenarios Rigorous simulations confirm the improved performance of our estimators in terms of bias and variance particularly in heavytailed contexts The practical implications of our findings are further illustrated through applications in reliability engineering and extreme value analysis This study contributes to the understanding of momentbased estimation in heavytailed distributions and offers a robust framework for statisticians dealing with data in the Weibull domain of attraction

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the integration of autoassociative models with generalized principal component analysis GPCA as a novel approach to dimensionality reduction and feature extraction in highdimensional data spaces Autoassociative models particularly those derived from neural network architectures provide a powerful framework for capturing intricate patterns and relationships within data by reconstructing inputs through latent representations We enhance this methodology by incorporating the principles of GPCA which enables the decomposition of data that lies on multiple subspaces thereby addressing the challenges posed by complex datasets characterized by heterogeneous structures Our proposed framework effectively utilizes the strengths of both paradigmsleveraging the capacity of autoassociative models to learn nonlinear mappings and the versatility of GPCA to represent multidimensional subspaces We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through comprehensive simulations and realworld applications showcasing improved performance in terms of reconstruction accuracy and interpretability This study contributes to the field of statistical learning by providing a coherent strategy for analyzing and visualizing complex data paving the way for future research in pattern recognition and exploratory data analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn recent years the proliferation of highdimensional data across various fields has necessitated the development of robust clustering methodologies that can effectively manage the complexities associated with highdimensional spaces This paper presents a comprehensive framework for highdimensional data clustering that integrates advanced statistical techniques with geometric insights We first explore the challenges inherent in clustering highdimensional data including the curse of dimensionality sparsity and the potential for noiseinduced artifacts in clustering results We propose a novel clustering algorithm that leverages a combination of dimensionality reduction methods and densitybased clustering approaches enhancing the ability to identify meaningful group structures within the data Extensive experiments are conducted on both synthetic and realworld datasets to evaluate the performance of the proposed method against existing clustering algorithms Our findings demonstrate improved accuracy and interpretability in clustering outcomes along with significant computational efficiency This work not only contributes to the foundational understanding of highdimensional clustering but also offers practical solutions for researchers and practitioners dealing with largescale data analysis The implications of our results extend to various domains including bioinformatics image processing and social network analysis where highdimensional data is prevalent

author: Stephane Girard
text: Abstract This paper explores the application of kernel smoothing techniques in extremal quantile regression a powerful approach for estimating the conditional quantiles of extreme events in quantitative data Traditional quantile regression methods often struggle to capture the tail behavior of distributions especially in the presence of high variability or skewness We propose a novel kernelbased estimator that smooths the quantile curves at the extremes allowing for more accurate and stable estimates of quantiles associated with rare events Our methodology is grounded in robust statistical principles and integrates adaptive bandwidth selection to enhance performance in sparse data scenarios We provide a comprehensive theoretical framework that includes consistency and asymptotic distribution of the proposed estimator Through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the advantages of kernel smoothing in improving the estimation accuracy of extremal quantiles over existing techniques The results indicate significant improvements in predictive performance for risk assessment and decisionmaking in fields such as finance environmental science and engineering By bridging kernel methods and quantile regression this work contributes to a deeper understanding of extreme phenomena and offers practical tools for researchers and practitioners dealing with highstakes data

author: Stephane Girard
text: Abstract In the realm of multivariate response analysis traditional regression techniques often struggle to effectively capture the intricate relationships between predictors and multiple output variables This study introduces a novel Sliced Inverse Regression SIR method tailored specifically for scenarios involving multiple responses Our approach extends the classic SIR framework leveraging slice sampling techniques to reveal the underlying structure of multivariate data We demonstrate how this new methodology can efficiently identify the direction of maximum variability in the response variables while accounting for potential interdependencies among them Through theoretical derivations we establish the consistency and asymptotic properties of our proposed method We also provide empirical validation using both simulated datasets and realworld applications highlighting its superior performance compared to existing multivariate regression techniques in terms of prediction accuracy and interpretability This new SIR method not only enhances the understanding of complex multivariate relationships but also offers a robust framework for future research in statistical modeling of correlated responses

author: Stephane Girard
text: Abstract In the realm of extreme value theory accurate estimation of the conditional tail index is crucial for assessing the risk of rare events This paper introduces a novel moving window approach for the nonparametric estimation of the conditional tail index which addresses limitations in traditional methods that often rely on fixed data windows and parametric assumptions Our methodology employs adaptive sampling within sliding windows that dynamically adjust based on local data characteristics thereby enhancing the robustness and flexibility of tail index estimation We provide a comprehensive theoretical foundation for our approach establishing its consistency and asymptotic properties under various conditions Through extensive simulation studies and empirical applications we demonstrate that the moving window technique substantially improves estimation accuracy particularly in datasets exhibiting nonstationarity and volatility Our findings indicate that this innovative method not only outperforms existing nonparametric techniques but also offers valuable insights for practitioners in fields such as finance environmental science and risk management where understanding extreme behavior is essential

author: Stephane Girard
text: A semiparametric regression model of a qdimensional multivariate response y on a pdimensional covariate x is considered A new approach is proposed based on sliced inverse regression SIR for estimating the effective dimension reduction EDR space without requiring a prespecified parametric model The convergence at rate root n of the estimated EDR space is shown The choice of the dimension of the EDR space is discussed Moreover a way to cluster components of y related to the same EDR space is provided Thus the proposed multivariate SIR method can be used properly on each cluster instead of blindly applying it on all components of y The numerical performances of multivariate SIR are illustrated on a simulation study An application to the Minneapolis elementary schools data is also provided Although the proposed methodology relies on SIR it opens the door for new regression approaches with a multivariate response They could be built similarly based on other reduction dimension methods C Elsevier BV All rights

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the estimation of extreme quantiles for Weibull tail distributions which are widely used in reliability engineering survival analysis and risk management Given the importance of accurately estimating these quantiles in highrisk scenarios we present a robust methodology that combines maximum likelihood estimation MLE with advanced bootstrap techniques to enhance precision and reliability We begin by outlining the theoretical underpinnings of Weibull distribution properties particularly focusing on its tail behavior and the implications for extreme value theory Using extensive simulations we compare the performance of our proposed method against traditional estimation techniques highlighting the improvements in accuracy and confidence interval coverage Additionally we apply our methodology to realworld datasets to demonstrate its practical applicability in various fields including environmental science and finance Our findings reveal significant advancements in the estimation of extreme quantiles ultimately providing practitioners with more reliable tools for risk assessment and decisionmaking in uncertain environments This paper contributes to the growing body of literature on extreme value estimation offering a pathway for future research into robust statistical methods for complex distributions

author: Stephane Girard
text: We address the problem of estimating the edge of a bounded set in d given a random set of points drawn from the interior Our method is based on a transformation of estimators dedicated to uniform point processes and obtained by smoothing some of its bias corrected extreme points An application to the estimation of starshaped supports is presented

author: Stephane Girard
text: This article proposes simple estimation methods dedicated to a semiparametric family of bivariate copulas These copulas can be simply estimated through the estimation of their univariate generating function We use this result to estimate the associated measures of association as well as the high probability regions of the copula These procedures are illustrated using both simulations and real data

author: Stephane Girard
text: In a previous paper Girard S Jacob P Extreme values and kernel estimates of point processes boundaries ESAIM Probability and Statistics we studied a kernel estimate of the upper edge of a twodimensional bounded set based upon the extreme values of a Poisson point process The initial paper Geffroy J Sur un probleme destimation geometrique Publications de lInstitut de Statistique de lUniversite de Paris XIII on the subject treats the frontier as the boundary of the support set for a density and the points as a random sample We claimed in our paper cited above that we are able to deduce the random sample case from the point process case The present note gives some essential indications to this end including a method which can be of general interest C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: In Gardes et al a new family of distributions is introduced depending on two parameters tau and theta which encompasses Paretotype distributions as well as Weibull taildistributions Estimators for theta and extreme quantiles are also proposed but they both depend on the unknown parameter tau making them useless in practical situations In this paper we propose an estimator of tau which is independent of theta Plugging our estimator of tau in the two previous ones allows us to estimate extreme quantiles from Paretotype and Weibull taildistributions in an unified way The asymptotic distributions of our three new estimators are established and their efficiency is illustrated on a small simulation study and on a real data set C Elsevier BV

author: Stephane Girard
text: Copulas are a useful tool to model multivariate distributions While there exist various families of bivariate copulas much less work has been done when the dimension is higher We propose a class of multivariate copulas based on products of transformed bivariate copulas The analytical forms of the copulas within this class allow to naturally associate a graphical structure which helps to visualize the dependencies and to compute the full joint likelihood even in high dimension Numerical experiments are conducted both on simulated and real data thanks to a dedicated R package C Elsevier Inc All rights

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractThis paper explores the estimation of extreme quantiles from both heavytailed and lighttailed distributions which are critical for risk assessment and decisionmaking in various fields including finance environmental science and telecommunications We begin by discussing the theoretical underpinnings of extreme value theory EVT and its application to different tail behaviors We propose a comprehensive framework that compares several estimation methods including the Peak Over Threshold POT approach the Block Maximum method and the application of generalized Pareto and Gumbel distributions Through extensive simulation studies we investigate the performance of these methods in terms of bias variance and confidence interval coverage across diverse tail characteristics Our findings highlight the strengths and weaknesses of each technique in estimating extreme quantiles under varying sample sizes and distributional conditions We also provide practical guidelines for practitioners to select appropriate methods based on the specific characteristics of the data Ultimately this study contributes to the understanding and application of extreme value methodologies enhancing the predictive capabilities for extreme events in both heavy and lighttailed contexts

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a new class of multivariate copulas constructed through the product of bivariate copulas expanding the toolkit available for modeling dependent structures in multivariate data Our approach leverages the flexibility and interpretability of bivariate copulas allowing for the systematic generation of copulas in higher dimensions while maintaining their essential properties We provide a comprehensive framework for defining and analyzing these copulas including conditions for their validity and methods for parameter estimation We illustrate the practical applicability of our proposed class through a series of simulation studies and empirical examples demonstrating its advantages in capturing complex dependencies across multiple variables Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings for the fields of finance hydrology and environmental science where understanding multivariate dependencies is critical Our results highlight the potential for this novel class of copulas to enhance statistical modeling and improve inference in realworld applications

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic behavior of extreme values associated with point processes and their implications for boundary estimations using Haar series By employing advanced statistical methods we derive estimates for the boundaries of point processes based on extreme value theory offering a novel perspective on how these boundaries can be more accurately delineated We present a comprehensive analysis of the convergence properties of Haar series as they relate to stochastic point processes providing insights into the estimation of boundary behavior in highdimensional settings The theoretical findings are bolstered by simulation studies that demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods in both synthetic and realworld data applications Our results reveal that incorporating extreme value considerations into Haar series estimations significantly improves the robustness and precision of boundary estimates offering a valuable framework for researchers and practitioners dealing with complex highdimensional point process data

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a novel methodology for estimating the boundaries of nonuniform point processes using smoothed extreme value estimators Our approach capitalizes on the unique properties of extreme value theory to enhance estimation accuracy in the presence of sparsely distributed data We specifically focus on the estimation of starshaped supports which are prevalent in various scientific fields including ecology astrophysics and material sciences We demonstrate how our smoothed extreme value estimators effectively capture the underlying boundary characteristics while mitigating the influence of noise and irregularities in the data Through a series of simulations and realworld applications we compare our method against traditional boundary estimation techniques showcasing improved performance in terms of bias variance and computational efficiency Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of point process boundaries and offer a robust framework for tasks requiring precise geometric estimations in complex environments This work provides a significant advance in the statistical treatment of nonuniform point processes and has implications for further research in boundary estimation and spatial data analysis

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore the relationship between extreme value theory and kernel density estimators with a focus on their application to sample boundaries We introduce a novel approach that leverages kernel estimators to accurately estimate the boundaries of a sample distribution particularly in the presence of extreme values that can skew traditional analyses By analyzing various kernel functions and bandwidth selection techniques we demonstrate how these methods can improve the identification of extreme quantiles and provide robust boundary estimates We provide theoretical insights into the asymptotic properties of our proposed estimators and illustrate their practical effectiveness using simulated datasets and realworld applications Our findings highlight the importance of integrating extreme value considerations into the framework of kernel estimation offering new pathways for researchers in fields reliant on accurate boundary assessment such as finance environmental science and reliability engineering

author: Stephane Girard
text: Abstract In this paper we propose novel estimation procedures for a semiparametric family of bivariate copulas aiming to enhance the modeling of dependence structures in multivariate data Our approach integrates parametric and nonparametric elements allowing for greater flexibility in capturing both linear and nonlinear dependencies We derive the theoretical properties of the proposed estimators including consistency and asymptotic normality and demonstrate their effectiveness through comprehensive simulation studies To illustrate practical applications we analyze realworld datasets from finance and environmental science where traditional copula models may fall short Our results indicate that the semiparametric estimation procedures outperform conventional methods in terms of fit and predictive accuracy This work contributes to the growing field of copula modeling by providing robust tools for statisticians and data analysts to better understand complex bivariate relationships

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a new method for estimating the edge of a twodimensional bounded set given a finite random set of points drawn from the interior The estimator is based both on Haar series and extreme values of the point process We give conditions for various kind of convergence and we obtain remarkably different possible limit distributions We propose a method of reducing the negative bias illustrated by a simulation

author: Stephane Girard
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of the L error associated with a boundary estimator in nonparametric statistics Specifically we examine the estimation of boundaries in highdimensional data scenarios where traditional methods may fail due to the curse of dimensionality We establish conditions under which the L error of the proposed boundary estimator converges in distribution to a normal distribution as the sample size approaches infinity Our results leverage techniques from empirical process theory and concentration inequalities to derive convergence rates and moments of the estimator We show that our estimator maintains robust performance even under varying smoothness conditions of the boundary functions Moreover we provide simulations and real data applications to illustrate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings emphasizing the practical implications for boundary estimation in diverse statistical modeling contexts This work contributes to the broader understanding of boundary behavior in nonparametric settings and offers new avenues for improvement in boundary estimation techniques

author: Stephane Girard
text: We present a result on the asymptotic normality of the Lerror of the suppiecewise constant estimator of frontier functions This result is obtained by means of an original squeezing method of the empirical point process between two Poisson point processes The result is available under the best rate of convergence but becomes fully useful under suboptimal conditions
